title: Formally smooth for an adic topology on the target
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, making $S$ an $R$-algebra, and $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ an ideal. $S$ is *formally smooth over $R$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology* (also: $\varphi$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology) if the following lifting property holds: for every commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, every ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, with quotient map $q:D\to D/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and every homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:S\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Remarks (proved in the steps below; not part of the condition): (a) such an $f$ satisfies $f(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$; (b) for a homomorphism $g:S\to E$ into any ring $E$, '$g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$' says exactly that $g$ is continuous for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology on $S$ and the discrete topology on $E$ (Stacks, Lemma 07E9), so the condition is Stacks More on Algebra, Definition 07EB for $R$ with the discrete topology, $S$ with the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology and $D$ discrete, by (a) with $f$ continuous. Explanatory note (not used in the DAG, not proved here): by Stacks Lemma 07EC(2) the same condition is obtained when $R$ carries the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology for an ideal $\mathfrak m\subseteq R$ with $\varphi(\mathfrak m^e)\subseteq\mathfrak n$ for some $e\ge1$; Stacks Definition 07NI calls these equivalent conditions 'formally smooth for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology'. The DAG uses the condition as written above (the case $\mathfrak m=0$ of 07NI).

proof.text: *The definition is well formed; remark (a).* $R$-algebras, their homomorphisms, the quotient $R$-algebra $D/J$ with the $R$-algebra map $q$, and the powers $\mathfrak n^k$, $J^2$ are [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The condition quantifies over rings $D$, ideals $J$ and maps $g$ and asks for the existence of $f$; no choice is made, so it is a property of the pair $(\varphi,\mathfrak n)$. It depends only on the isomorphism class of $S$ as an $R$-algebra together with $\mathfrak n$ (transport $g$ and $f$ along an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:S'\to S$ with $\alpha(\mathfrak n')=\mathfrak n$, which carries $\mathfrak n'^k$ onto $\mathfrak n^k$). Remark (a): let $f$ be a lift of $g$ with $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$. For $x\in\mathfrak n^k$, $q(f(x))=g(x)=0$, so $f(\mathfrak n^k)\subseteq\ker q=J$. The ideal $\mathfrak n^{2k}=\mathfrak n^k\mathfrak n^k$ is generated by products $xy$ with $x,y\in\mathfrak n^k$, and $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)\in J\cdot J=J^2=0$; as $f$ is additive and $f(sz)=f(s)f(z)$, the set of $z$ with $f(z)=0$ contains these generators and is closed under sums and $S$-multiples, so $f(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$. This is the argument of the proof of Lemma 07EC(1): '$\psi(\mathfrak n^k)\subset J$ hence $\psi(\mathfrak n^{2k})=0$ as $J^2=0$'.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165), proof of part (1) (lines 9184-9197)

proof.text: *Remark (b): continuity for adic and discrete topologies.* The $\mathfrak n$-adic topology on $S$ is the topology for which the sets $s+\mathfrak n^k$ ($s\in S$, $k\ge1$) form a basis; it makes $S$ a topological ring, and the $\mathfrak n^k$ are a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of $0$ (More on Algebra, Section 07E7, 'adic topology', with $\mathfrak n^0=S$ and $\mathfrak n^{k+1}\subseteq\mathfrak n^k$). Let $g:S\to E$ be a ring homomorphism, $E$ discrete. If $g$ is continuous, $g^{-1}(\{0\})=\ker g$ is open and contains $0$, so it contains a basic neighbourhood $\mathfrak n^k$ ($k\ge1$ after enlarging $k$), i.e. $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$. Conversely, if $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$, then for any subset $U\subseteq E$, $g^{-1}(U)$ is a union of cosets $s+\ker g$, and $s+\ker g=\bigcup_{t\in s+\ker g}(t+\mathfrak n^k)$ is open, so $g$ is continuous. This is Lemma 07E9 for the ideals $\mathfrak n\subseteq S$ and $0\subseteq E$ (the discrete topology is the $0$-adic topology; Stacks omits the proof). With $R$ discrete every ring map out of $R$ is continuous, and $D$, $D/J$ discrete (the quotient topology of a discrete ring is discrete), so a commutative diagram of homomorphisms of topological rings as in Definition 07EB is exactly the data $R\to D$, $J$ with $J^2=0$, and an $R$-algebra map $g:S\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak n^k)=0$; a dotted arrow of 07EB is an $R$-algebra map $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$ that is continuous, and by step 1 and the first part every lift is continuous. Hence the condition agrees with Definition 07EB for these topologies.
